verses.text: The book of the generation (family line) of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Abraham was the father of Isaac. Isaac was the father of Jacob. Jacob was the father of Judah and his brothers.
Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah. Their mother was Tamar. Perez was the father of Hezron. Hezron was the father of Ram.
Ram was the father of Amminadab. Amminadab was the father of Nahshon. Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
Salmon was the father of Boaz. Boaz's mother was Rahab. Boaz was the father of Obed. Obed's mother was Ruth. Obed was the father of Jesse.
Jesse was the father of David the king. David the king was the father of Solomon. Solomon's mother had been the wife of Uriah.
Solomon was the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam was the father of Abijah. Abijah was the father of Asa.
Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat was the father of Joram. Joram was the father of Uzziah.
Uzziah was the father of Jotham. Jotham was the father of Ahaz. Ahaz was the father of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh. Manasseh was the father of Amon. Amon was the father of Josiah.
Josiah was the father of Jeconiah and his brothers, about the time they were carried away to Babylon.
After they were brought to Babylon, Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel was the father of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud. Abiud was the father of Eliakim. Eliakim was the father of Azor.
Azor was the father of Sadoc. Sadoc was the father of Achim. Achim was the father of Eliud.
Eliud was the father of Eleazar. Eleazar was the father of Matthan. Matthan was the father of Jacob.
Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary. Mary was the mother of Jesus, who is called Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David are 14 generations. From David to the time they were carried away to Babylon are 14 generations. From the time they were carried away to Babylon to Christ are 14 generations.
Now the birth of Jesus Christ happened like this. His mother Mary was engaged to Joseph. Before Joseph and Mary came together, Mary was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit.
Joseph her husband was a just (good and fair) man. Joseph did not want to make her a public example (shame her in public). So Joseph planned to put her away (end the engagement) secretly.

But while Joseph thought about these things, the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. The angel said: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The child in her is from the Holy Spirit.
Mary will give birth to a son, and you will name Him JESUS. For He will save His people from their sins.
All this was done so that what the Lord said by the prophet would come true:
Look, a virgin will be with child, and will give birth to a son. They will call His name Emmanuel, which means: God with us.
Then Joseph woke up from sleep. Joseph did what the angel of the Lord had told him, and took Mary as his wife.
Joseph did not know her (have relations with her) until she had given birth to her firstborn son. And Joseph named Him JESUS.

1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences): v25 restores 'her firstborn son'; familiar forms of the names in the family line. Earlier notes: V18 names Joseph and Mary explicitly rather than leaving them as 'he/she' at the point of highest ambiguity in the passage. V21 restores that the angel is directly commanding Joseph ('thou shalt call his name JESUS') to name the child -- the earlier passive 'his name must be Jesus' lost who was actually being addressed, which matters since Joseph's act of naming is what legally adopts Jesus into David's throne line.

verses.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king. Then wise men from the east came to Jerusalem.
The wise men said: Where is He who is born King of the Jews? For we have seen His star in the east, and we have come to worship Him.
When Herod the king heard this, Herod was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Herod gathered all the chief priests and scribes (teachers of the law) of the people together. Herod asked them where Christ would be born.
They said to Herod: In Bethlehem of Judea. For this is what the prophet wrote:
And you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are not the least among the princes of Judah. For out of you will come a Governor, who will rule My people Israel.
Then Herod secretly called the wise men. Herod carefully asked them what time the star appeared.
Herod sent them to Bethlehem and said: Go and search carefully for the young child. When you have found Him, bring me word, so that I may come and worship Him also.
When the wise men had heard the king, they left. And the star they saw in the east went before them, until it came and stood over where the young child was.
When the wise men saw the star, they rejoiced with very great joy.
When the wise men came into the house, they saw the young child with Mary His mother. They fell down and worshipped Him. They opened their treasures and gave Him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
God warned the wise men in a dream that they should not go back to Herod. So they went back to their own country another way.

When the wise men had left, the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream. The angel said: Get up. Take the young child and His mother and run away to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod will look for the young child to destroy Him.
Joseph got up and took the young child and His mother by night, and left for Egypt.
Joseph stayed there until the death of Herod. This was so that what the Lord said by the prophet would come true: Out of Egypt I have called My Son.

Herod saw that the wise men had mocked (tricked) him, and Herod was very angry. Herod sent soldiers and killed all the children in Bethlehem and all the land around it, from 2 years old and under. This was by the time Herod had carefully asked the wise men.
Then what Jeremiah the prophet said came true:
In Ramah a voice was heard: lamentation (loud crying), weeping, and great mourning. Rachel was weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are no more.
But when Herod was dead, the angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.
The angel said: Get up. Take the young child and His mother, and go into the land of Israel. For those who wanted to kill the young child are dead.
Joseph got up and took the young child and His mother, and came into the land of Israel.
But Joseph heard that Archelaus ruled in Judea in place of his father Herod. Joseph was afraid to go there. God warned Joseph in a dream, so Joseph went into the area of Galilee.
Joseph came and lived in a city called Nazareth. This was so that what the prophets said would come true: He will be called a Nazarene.

verses.text: In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness (desert) of Judea.
John said: Repent (change your heart), for the kingdom of heaven is at hand (near).
John is the one the prophet Isaiah spoke about: The voice of one crying in the wilderness (desert): Prepare the way of the Lord. Make His paths straight.
John wore clothes of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem, all Judea, and all the area around the Jordan went out to John.
They were baptized by John in the Jordan, confessing their sins.

But John saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism. John said to them: O generation (family) of vipers (poisonous snakes), who warned you to run from the wrath (God's anger) to come?
So bring forth fruits that show you have repented (changed your heart).
Do not think to say within yourselves: We have Abraham as our father. For I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.
And now also the ax is laid to the root of the trees. So every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

I indeed baptize you with water to repentance (a change of heart). But the One who comes after me is mightier than I am. I am not worthy to carry His shoes. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His fan (winnowing tool) is in His hand. He will clean His threshing floor completely. He will gather His wheat into the barn, but He will burn up the chaff (husks) with fire that cannot be put out.
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by John.
But John tried to stop Jesus. John said: I need to be baptized by You, and You come to me?
Jesus answered John: Let it be so now, for this is the right way for us to fulfill all righteousness (being right with God). Then John let Jesus be baptized.
When Jesus was baptized, He came up right away out of the water. And the heavens were opened to Him. He saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and lighting on Him.
And a voice from heaven said: This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness (desert) to be tempted by the devil.
Jesus fasted (went without food) 40 days and 40 nights. Afterward He was hungry.
When the tempter came to Jesus, the tempter said: If You are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.
But Jesus answered: It is written: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes out of the mouth of God.
Then the devil took Jesus up into the holy city. The devil set Jesus on a pinnacle (high point) of the temple.

The devil said to Jesus: If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down. For it is written: He will give His angels charge over You. In their hands they will hold You up, so that You do not hit Your foot against a stone.
Jesus said to the devil: It is written again: You shall not tempt (test) the Lord your God.
Again, the devil took Jesus up into a very high mountain. The devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.
The devil said to Jesus: I will give You all these things, if You will fall down and worship me.
Then Jesus said to the devil: Get away from here, Satan. For it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve.
Then the devil left Jesus. And angels came and ministered to (served) Jesus.
Now when Jesus heard that John was put in prison, Jesus went into Galilee.
Jesus left Nazareth and came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the land of Zebulun and Naphtali.
This was so that what Isaiah the prophet said would come true:
The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews):
The people who sat in darkness saw a great light. And to those who sat in the region and shadow of death, light has sprung up.
From that time Jesus began to preach and to say: Repent (change your heart), for the kingdom of heaven is at hand (near).
Jesus was walking by the Sea of Galilee. Jesus saw two brothers, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother. They were throwing a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them: Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.
Right away they left their nets and followed Jesus.
Jesus went on from there and saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother. They were in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. Jesus called them.
Right away they left the ship and their father, and followed Jesus.

Jesus went all around Galilee. Jesus taught in their synagogues (meeting houses) and preached the good news of the kingdom. Jesus healed all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease among the people.

The fame of Jesus went through all Syria. They brought to Jesus all the sick people who had different diseases and pains. They brought those who were possessed with devils (demons), those who were lunatic (had seizures), and those who had palsy (could not move their bodies). And Jesus healed them.
Great crowds of people followed Jesus from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from beyond Jordan.

verses.text: Jesus saw the crowds of people, and He went up into a mountain. When He sat down, His disciples came to Him.
Jesus opened His mouth and taught them. Jesus said:
Blessed are the poor in spirit (humble before God), for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are those who mourn (are very sad), for they will be comforted.
Blessed are the meek (gentle), for they will inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness (being right with God), for they will be filled.
Blessed are the merciful, for they will receive mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called the children of God.
Blessed are those who are persecuted (attacked) for righteousness' (being right with God) sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are you when people revile (insult) you and persecute (attack) you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for My sake.
Rejoice, and be very glad, for your reward in heaven is great. For that is how they persecuted (attacked) the prophets who were before you.
You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt has lost its savor (taste), how can it be made salty again? From then on it is good for nothing, except to be thrown out and walked on by people.
You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden.
People do not light a candle and put it under a bushel (basket). They put it on a candlestick (lamp stand), and it gives light to everyone in the house.
Let your light shine before people in the same way. Then they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
Do not think that I have come to destroy the law or the prophets. I have not come to destroy, but to fulfill.
For truly I say to you: Until heaven and earth pass away, one jot (smallest letter) or one tittle (smallest mark) will in no way pass from the law, until all is fulfilled.

So whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments, and teaches people to do so, will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

For I say to you: Unless your righteousness (being right with God) is greater than the righteousness of the scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, you will in no way enter into the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said by them of old time: You shall not kill. And whoever kills will be in danger of the judgment.

But I say to you: Whoever is angry with their brother without a cause will be in danger of the judgment. Whoever says to their brother, Raca (worthless), will be in danger of the council (court). But whoever says, You fool, will be in danger of hell fire.
So if you bring your gift to the altar, and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled (make peace) with your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

Agree with your adversary (the one taking you to court) quickly, while you are on the way with him. Otherwise the adversary may hand you to the judge, and the judge may hand you to the officer, and you will be thrown into prison.
Truly I say to you: You will in no way come out of there until you have paid the last farthing (smallest coin).
You have heard that it was said by them of old time: You shall not commit adultery.
But I say to you: Whoever looks on a woman to lust (wrongly desire) after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

If your right eye offends you (causes you to sin), pluck it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you that one of your body parts should perish, than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.

And if your right hand offends you (causes you to sin), cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you that one of your body parts should perish, than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
It has been said: Whoever puts away (divorces) his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement (written divorce paper).
But I say to you: Whoever puts away (divorces) his wife, except for the cause of fornication (sexual sin), causes her to commit adultery. And whoever marries her that is divorced commits adultery.
Again, you have heard that it was said by them of old time: You shall not forswear yourself (break a promise to God), but you shall keep your oaths (promises) to the Lord.
But I say to you: Swear not at all. Do not swear by heaven, for it is God's throne.
Do not swear by the earth, for it is His footstool. Do not swear by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Do not swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let your communication (speaking) be: Yes, yes; No, no. For whatever is more than these comes from evil.
You have heard that it has been said: An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.
But I say to you: Do not resist evil. Whoever hits you on your right cheek, turn to him the other cheek also.
If anyone takes you to court and takes away your coat, let him have your cloak (outer coat) also.
Whoever forces you to go a mile, go with him two miles.
Give to anyone who asks you. And from anyone who wants to borrow from you, do not turn away.
You have heard that it has been said: You shall love your neighbor, and hate your enemy.
But I say to you: Love your enemies. Bless those who curse you. Do good to those who hate you. And pray for those who despitefully use (mistreat) you and persecute (attack) you.
Then you may be the children of your Father who is in heaven. For He makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good. And He sends rain on the just and on the unjust.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the publicans (tax collectors) do the same?
And if you greet your brothers only, what do you do more than others? Do not even the publicans (tax collectors) do so?
So be perfect, even as your Father who is in heaven is perfect.

verses.text: Be careful that you do not do your alms (gifts to the poor) in front of people, to be seen by them. If you do, you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.

So when you give alms (gifts to the poor), do not blow a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites (pretenders) do in the synagogues (meeting houses) and in the streets, so that people will praise them. Truly I say to you: They have their reward.
But when you give alms (gifts to the poor), do not let your left hand know what your right hand does.
Then your alms (gifts to the poor) will be in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you openly.

And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites (pretenders). They love to pray standing in the synagogues (meeting houses) and on the corners of the streets, so that people will see them. Truly I say to you: They have their reward.
But when you pray, go into your room. When you have shut your door, pray to your Father, who is in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you openly.
But when you pray, do not use vain repetitions (the same empty words again and again), as the heathen (people who do not know God) do. They think they will be heard because they speak many words.
So do not be like them. For your Father knows what things you need before you ask Him.
So pray in this way: Our Father who is in heaven, hallowed (holy) be Your name.
Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread.
And forgive us our debts (sins), as we forgive our debtors (those who sin against us).
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For Yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.
For if you forgive people their trespasses (wrongs), your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
But if you do not forgive people their trespasses (wrongs), neither will your Father forgive your trespasses (wrongs).

Also, when you fast (go without food), do not be like the hypocrites (pretenders), with a sad face. They make their faces look gloomy, so that people will see they are fasting. Truly I say to you: They have their reward.
But when you fast (go without food), anoint (put oil on) your head, and wash your face.
Then you will not look to people like you are fasting, but only to your Father, who is in secret. And your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you openly.
Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not break in or steal.
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
The light of the body is the eye. So if your eye is single (clear and focused), your whole body will be full of light.
But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. So if the light that is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness.
No one can serve two masters. Either that person will hate the one and love the other, or else hold to the one and despise (look down on) the other. You cannot serve God and mammon (money).

So I say to you: Take no thought (do not worry) for your life, what you will eat or what you will drink. Do not worry for your body, what you will wear. Is not the life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
Look at the birds of the air. They do not sow, or reap, or gather into barns. Yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much better than they are?
Which of you by taking thought (worrying) can add one cubit (about 18 inches) to your height?
And why do you take thought (worry) about clothes? Think about the lilies of the field, how they grow. They do not work, and they do not spin cloth.
And yet I say to you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
So if God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?
So take no thought (do not worry), saying: What will we eat? or, What will we drink? or, What will we wear?
For the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) seek after all these things. And your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first the kingdom of God, and His righteousness (being right with God), and all these things will be added to you.
So take no thought (do not worry) for tomorrow. Tomorrow will take thought for the things of itself. Each day has enough evil (trouble) of its own.
Judge not, so that you are not judged.
For with the judgment you judge, you will be judged. And with the measure you use, it will be measured to you again.
Why do you look at the mote (speck of dust) that is in your brother's eye, but do not think about the beam (big piece of wood) that is in your own eye?
How can you say to your brother: Let me pull the mote (speck of dust) out of your eye? And look, a beam (big piece of wood) is in your own eye.
You hypocrite (pretender), first take the beam (big piece of wood) out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly to take the mote (speck of dust) out of your brother's eye.
Do not give what is holy to the dogs. Do not throw your pearls before swine (pigs). Otherwise they will trample them under their feet, and turn again and tear you.
Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives. The one who seeks finds. And to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Or what man is there among you, who would give his son a stone if his son asks for bread?
Or if his son asks for a fish, will he give his son a serpent (snake)?
So if you, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask Him?
So whatever you want people to do to you, do the same to them. For this is the law and the prophets.
Enter in at the strait (narrow) gate. For wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction. And many go in that way.
For strait (narrow) is the gate, and narrow is the way, that leads to life. And few find it.
Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep's clothing, but inside they are ravening (hungry, killing) wolves.
You will know them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
In the same way, every good tree brings forth good fruit. But a corrupt (rotten) tree brings forth evil fruit.
A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit. And a corrupt (rotten) tree cannot bring forth good fruit.
Every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So by their fruits you will know them.
Not everyone who says to Me: Lord, Lord, will enter into the kingdom of heaven. Only the one who does the will of My Father who is in heaven will enter.
Many will say to Me in that day: Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name? And in Your name have we not cast out devils (demons)? And in Your name done many wonderful works?
And then I will tell them plainly: I never knew you. Depart from Me, you who work iniquity (sin).
So whoever hears these sayings of Mine, and does them, I will compare to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
The rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house. And it did not fall, for it was founded on a rock.
And everyone who hears these sayings of Mine, and does not do them, will be like a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.
The rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house. And it fell, and great was the fall of it.
When Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished (amazed) at His doctrine (teaching).
For Jesus taught them as One having authority, and not as the scribes (teachers of the law).

verses.text: When Jesus came down from the mountain, great multitudes (large crowds) followed Him.
And look, a leper (a man with a skin disease) came and worshipped Jesus. The leper said: Lord, if You will, You can make me clean.
Jesus put out His hand and touched the leper. Jesus said: I will. Be clean. And right away his leprosy (skin disease) was cleansed (healed).
Jesus said to the man: See that you tell no one. But go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony (proof) to them.
When Jesus entered Capernaum, a centurion (army officer over 100 soldiers) came to Jesus and begged Him.
The centurion said: Lord, my servant is lying at home sick with palsy (could not move his body). He is suffering terribly.
Jesus said to the centurion: I will come and heal him.
The centurion answered: Lord, I am not worthy for You to come under my roof. But speak the word only, and my servant will be healed.
For I am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this man, Go, and he goes. I say to another, Come, and he comes. I say to my servant, Do this, and he does it.
When Jesus heard this, He marvelled (was amazed). Jesus said to those who followed: Truly I say to you: I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel.
And I say to you: Many will come from the east and west. They will sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
But the children of the kingdom will be thrown out into outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing (grinding) of teeth.
Jesus said to the centurion: Go your way. As you have believed, so it will be done for you. And his servant was healed in that same hour.
When Jesus came into Peter's house, Jesus saw Peter's wife's mother lying in bed, sick with a fever.
Jesus touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and ministered to (served) them.
When evening came, people brought to Jesus many who were possessed with devils (demons). Jesus cast out (drove out) the spirits with His word, and healed all who were sick.
This happened so that what was spoken by Esaias (Isaiah) the prophet would be fulfilled (come true). Isaiah said: He Himself took our infirmities (weaknesses), and carried our sicknesses.
When Jesus saw great multitudes (large crowds) around Him, He gave a command to go over to the other side of the lake.
A scribe (teacher of the law) came and said to Jesus: Master (Teacher), I will follow You wherever You go.
Jesus said to the scribe: The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests. But the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.
Another of His disciples said to Jesus: Lord, suffer (allow) me first to go and bury my father.
But Jesus said to him: Follow Me. Let the dead bury their dead.
Jesus got into a ship (boat), and His disciples followed Him.
And look, a great tempest (storm) came up on the sea. The waves covered the ship (boat). But Jesus was asleep.
His disciples came to Jesus and woke Him up. They said: Lord, save us. We perish (are dying).
Jesus said to them: Why are you fearful, you of little faith? Then Jesus got up and rebuked (gave a strong command to) the winds and the sea. And there was a great calm.
But the men marvelled (were amazed). They said: What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey Him!

Jesus came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes. Two men possessed with devils (demons) met Jesus. They came out of the tombs. They were very fierce (wild and dangerous), so that no one could pass by that way.
And look, the two men cried out: What do we have to do with You, Jesus, You Son of God? Have You come here to torment (hurt) us before the time?
A good distance away from them, a herd of many swine (pigs) was feeding.
So the devils (demons) begged Jesus: If You cast us out, suffer (allow) us to go away into the herd of swine (pigs).

Jesus said to them: Go. When the devils (demons) came out of the men, they went into the herd of swine (pigs). And look, the whole herd of swine (pigs) ran fast down a steep place into the sea, and died in the waters.
The men who kept the swine (pigs) ran away. They went into the city and told everything, and what had happened to the men who had been possessed with devils (demons).
And look, the whole city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw Jesus, they begged Him to leave their coasts (land).

9.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. leaving out "to repentance" in 9:13 and "they fainted" in 9:36), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Jesus entered into a ship (boat), passed over the lake, and came into His own city.

And look, they brought to Jesus a man sick with palsy (could not move his body), lying on a bed. Jesus saw their faith. Jesus said to the man with palsy (could not move his body): Son, be of good cheer (be happy). Your sins are forgiven you.
And look, some of the scribes (teachers of the law) said within themselves: This man blasphemes (speaks against God).
Jesus knew their thoughts. Jesus said: Why do you think evil in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say: Your sins are forgiven you? Or to say: Get up, and walk?

But this is so that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins. Then Jesus said to the man with palsy (could not move his body): Get up, take up your bed, and go to your house.
And the man got up, and went to his house.
When the multitudes (large crowds) saw it, they marvelled (were amazed). They glorified (praised) God, who had given such power to men.
As Jesus went on from there, He saw a man named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom (tax booth). Jesus said to Matthew: Follow Me. And Matthew got up and followed Jesus.
Jesus sat at meat (ate a meal) in the house. And look, many publicans (tax collectors) and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and His disciples.
When the Pharisees saw it, they said to His disciples: Why does your Master (Teacher) eat with publicans (tax collectors) and sinners?
When Jesus heard that, He said to them: Those who are whole (healthy) do not need a physician (doctor), but those who are sick.
But go and learn what this means: I will have mercy, and not sacrifice. For I have not come to call the righteous (those who are right with God), but sinners to repentance (a change of heart).
Then the disciples of John came to Jesus. They said: Why do we and the Pharisees fast (go without food) often, but Your disciples do not fast (go without food)?

Jesus said to them: Can the children of the bridechamber (friends of the bridegroom) mourn (be very sad) while the bridegroom (the man getting married) is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them. Then they will fast (go without food).
No one puts a piece of new cloth on an old garment (piece of clothing). The new piece pulls away from the garment, and the rent (tear) is made worse.

People do not put new wine into old bottles (leather wine bags). If they do, the bottles break, the wine runs out, and the bottles perish (are ruined). But they put new wine into new bottles (leather wine bags), and both are preserved (kept safe).
While Jesus spoke these things to them, look, a ruler came and worshipped Jesus. The ruler said: My daughter has just now died. But come and lay Your hand on her, and she will live.
Jesus got up and followed the ruler. And His disciples went too.
And look, a woman who had been sick with an issue of blood (bleeding) for twelve years came behind Jesus. She touched the hem (edge) of His garment (clothes).
For she said within herself: If I can only touch His garment (clothes), I will be whole (healed).
But Jesus turned around. When Jesus saw her, He said: Daughter, be of good comfort (take heart). Your faith has made you whole (healed). And the woman was made whole (healed) from that hour.
Jesus came into the ruler's house. Jesus saw the minstrels (musicians for the dead) and the people making a noise.
Jesus said to them: Give place (move away). For the maid (girl) is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed Jesus to scorn (laughed at Him).
When the people were put outside, Jesus went in. Jesus took her by the hand, and the maid (girl) got up.
And the fame (news) of this went out into all that land.
When Jesus left there, two blind men followed Him. They cried out: You Son of David, have mercy on us.
When Jesus came into the house, the blind men came to Him. Jesus said to them: Do you believe that I am able to do this? They said to Jesus: Yes, Lord.
Then Jesus touched their eyes. Jesus said: As your faith is, so let it be done to you.
And their eyes were opened. Jesus straitly charged (strongly warned) them: See that no one knows it.
But when the two men left, they spread His fame (news about Jesus) in all that country.
As they went out, look, people brought to Jesus a dumb (could not speak) man possessed with a devil (demon).
When the devil (demon) was cast out (driven out), the dumb (could not speak) man spoke. The multitudes (large crowds) marvelled (were amazed). They said: Nothing like this was ever seen in Israel.
But the Pharisees said: He casts out (drives out) devils (demons) through the prince (ruler) of the devils (demons).

Jesus went to all the cities and villages. Jesus taught in their synagogues (meeting houses), and preached the gospel (good news) of the kingdom. Jesus healed every sickness and every disease among the people.
When Jesus saw the multitudes (large crowds), He was moved with compassion (deep pity) for them. They fainted (were tired out) and were scattered, like sheep with no shepherd.
Then Jesus said to His disciples: The harvest truly is plenteous (very big), but the labourers (workers) are few.
So pray to the Lord of the harvest, that He will send out labourers (workers) into His harvest.
Jesus called His twelve disciples to Him. Jesus gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out (drive them out), and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease.
These are the names of the twelve apostles (sent ones): The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother. James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother.
Philip, and Bartholomew. Thomas, and Matthew the publican (tax collector). James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname (other name) was Thaddaeus.
Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed (handed over) Jesus.
Jesus sent out these twelve. Jesus commanded them: Do not go into the way of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). Do not enter into any city of the Samaritans.
But go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
As you go, preach this: The kingdom of heaven is at hand (near).
Heal the sick, cleanse (heal) the lepers (people with a skin disease), raise the dead, cast out (drive out) devils (demons). You received freely, so give freely.
Do not take gold, or silver, or brass (copper money) in your purses (money belts).
Do not take a scrip (traveling bag) for your trip, or two coats, or shoes, or staves (walking sticks). For the workman is worthy of his meat (has earned his food).
Whatever city or town you enter, ask who in it is worthy (good and ready to receive you). Stay there until you leave that place.
When you come into a house, salute it (greet the people there).
If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it. But if it is not worthy, let your peace come back to you.
Whoever will not receive you or hear your words, when you leave that house or city, shake off the dust from your feet.
Truly I say to you: It will be more tolerable (easier) for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.
Look, I send you out like sheep in the middle of wolves. So be wise as serpents (snakes), and harmless as doves.
But beware of men. For they will deliver you up (hand you over) to the councils (courts). They will scourge (whip) you in their synagogues (meeting houses).
You will be brought before governors and kings for My sake, for a testimony (proof) against them and the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).
But when they deliver you up (hand you over), take no thought (do not worry) how or what you will speak. For in that same hour it will be given to you what you will speak.
For it is not you who speak. It is the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
The brother will deliver up (hand over) the brother to death, and the father will hand over the child. The children will rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.
All people will hate you for My name's sake. But whoever endures (keeps on faithful) to the end will be saved.
When they persecute (attack) you in this city, flee into another. For truly I say to you: You will not have gone through all the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
The disciple is not above his master (teacher). The servant is not above his lord (master).

It is enough for the disciple to be like his master (teacher), and the servant like his lord (master). If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub (the devil), how much more will they call those of his household (family)?
So do not fear them. For there is nothing covered that will not be revealed (shown). And there is nothing hidden that will not be known.
What I tell you in darkness, speak in the light. What you hear in the ear, preach on the housetops.
Do not fear those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul. But fear Him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing (smallest coin)? Yet not one of them will fall on the ground without your Father.
But even the hairs of your head are all numbered (counted).
So do not fear. You are worth more than many sparrows.
Whoever confesses (says openly that they belong to) Me before men, I will also confess that person before My Father who is in heaven.
But whoever denies (says they do not know) Me before men, I will also deny that person before My Father who is in heaven.
Do not think that I have come to send peace on earth. I did not come to send peace, but a sword.
For I have come to set a man at variance (against each other) with his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
A man's foes (enemies) will be the people of his own household (family).
Whoever loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me. Whoever loves son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me.
Whoever does not take their cross and follow after Me is not worthy of Me.
Whoever finds their life will lose it. Whoever loses their life for My sake will find it.
Whoever receives you receives Me. And whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.

Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward. Whoever receives a righteous (right with God) man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man's reward.
Whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink, in the name of a disciple, truly I say to you: That person will in no way lose their reward.

verses.text: When Jesus had finished commanding His twelve disciples, Jesus left there to teach and to preach in their cities.
Now John was in prison. When John heard about the works of Christ, John sent two of his disciples.
They said to Jesus: Are You the One who should come, or do we look for another?
Jesus answered them: Go and show John again the things that you hear and see.

The blind receive their sight, and the lame (people who cannot walk well) walk. The lepers (people with a skin disease) are cleansed (healed), and the deaf hear. The dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel (good news) preached to them.
And blessed is whoever is not offended in Me (does not turn away because of Me).
As John's disciples left, Jesus began to speak to the multitudes (large crowds) about John: What did you go out into the wilderness (desert) to see? A reed (tall grass) shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft raiment (fine clothes)? Look, those who wear soft clothing are in kings' houses.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
For this is the one about whom it is written: Look, I send My messenger before Your face. He will prepare Your way before You.
Truly I say to you: Among those born of women, there has not risen anyone greater than John the Baptist. But whoever is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than John.
From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence (is attacked), and the violent take it by force.
For all the prophets and the law prophesied (spoke God's message) until John.
And if you will receive it, this is Elias (Elijah), who was to come.
Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
But what can I compare this generation (people living now) to? It is like children sitting in the markets, calling to their friends.
They say: We have piped (played the flute) for you, and you have not danced. We have mourned (shown great sadness) for you, and you have not lamented (cried).
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say: He has a devil (demon).

The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say: Look, a man who is gluttonous (eats too much), and a winebibber (drinks too much wine), a friend of publicans (tax collectors) and sinners. But wisdom is justified (shown to be right) by her children.
Then Jesus began to upbraid (scold) the cities where most of His mighty works were done, because they did not repent (change their hearts).

Woe (great trouble) to you, Chorazin! Woe (great trouble) to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented (changed their hearts) long ago in sackcloth (rough cloth worn when sorry) and ashes.
But I say to you: It will be more tolerable (easier) for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, which are exalted (lifted up) to heaven, will be brought down to hell. For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Sodom, Sodom would have remained until this day.
But I say to you: It will be more tolerable (easier) for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for you.

At that time Jesus answered: I thank You, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and prudent (clever), and have revealed (shown) them to babes (little children).
Yes, Father, for so it seemed good in Your sight.
All things are delivered (given) to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son, except the Father. And no one knows the Father, except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son will reveal (show) the Father.
Come to Me, all you who labour (work hard) and are heavy laden (carry heavy loads), and I will give you rest.
Take My yoke (wooden bar for working together) upon you, and learn from Me. For I am meek (gentle) and lowly (humble) in heart. And you will find rest for your souls.
For My yoke (wooden bar for working together) is easy, and My burden (load) is light.

12.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. leaving out "blind and" in 12:22 and "of the heart" in 12:35), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/him' rendered gender-neutral in v29, v35.

verses.text: At that time Jesus went through the corn (grain) fields on the sabbath day (day of rest). His disciples were hungry. They began to pluck the ears of corn (heads of grain) and to eat.
But when the Pharisees saw it, they said to Jesus: Look, Your disciples do what is not lawful (allowed by the law) to do on the sabbath day (day of rest).
But Jesus said to them: Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him?

David entered into the house of God, and ate the shewbread (holy bread set before God). It was not lawful (allowed by the law) for David to eat it, or for those who were with him, but only for the priests.
Or have you not read in the law, how on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane (break the rules of) the sabbath, and are blameless?
But I say to you: In this place is One greater than the temple.
But if you had known what this means, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned (judged guilty) the guiltless.
For the Son of Man is Lord even of the sabbath day (day of rest).
Jesus left there and went into their synagogue (meeting house).
And look, there was a man whose hand was withered (dried up and useless). They asked Jesus: Is it lawful (allowed by the law) to heal on the sabbath days? They asked so that they could accuse Jesus.
Jesus said to them: Which man among you has one sheep, and if it falls into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not take hold of it and lift it out?
How much better is a man than a sheep? So it is lawful (allowed by the law) to do good on the sabbath days.
Then Jesus said to the man: Stretch out your hand. And the man stretched it out. It was restored whole (healed), just like the other hand.
Then the Pharisees went out and held a council (meeting) against Jesus, to plan how they might destroy Him.
But when Jesus knew it, He withdrew (went away) from there. Great multitudes (large crowds) followed Him, and He healed them all.
Jesus charged (strongly told) them not to make Him known.
This happened so that what was spoken by Esaias (Isaiah) the prophet would be fulfilled (come true). Isaiah said:

Look at My servant, whom I have chosen. My beloved (dearly loved), in whom My soul is well pleased. I will put My Spirit upon Him, and He will show judgment (what is right) to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).
He will not strive (fight), or cry out. No one will hear His voice in the streets.
He will not break a bruised reed (bent grass). He will not quench (put out) smoking flax (a weak, smoking lamp wick), until He sends out judgment (what is right) to victory.
And the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) will trust in His name.
Then a man possessed with a devil (demon) was brought to Jesus. The man was blind and dumb (could not speak). Jesus healed him, so that the blind and dumb (could not speak) man both spoke and saw.
All the people were amazed. They said: Is not this the son of David?
But when the Pharisees heard it, they said: This fellow does not cast out (drive out) devils (demons) except by Beelzebub (the devil), the prince (ruler) of the devils (demons).
Jesus knew their thoughts. Jesus said to them: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation (ruin). Every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
If Satan casts out (drives out) Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
And if I cast out (drive out) devils (demons) by Beelzebub (the devil), by whom do your children cast them out? So they will be your judges.
But if I cast out (drive out) devils (demons) by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come to you.
Or how can anyone enter into a strong man's house and spoil (steal) his goods, unless that person first ties up the strong man? Then that person will spoil (rob) his house.
Whoever is not with Me is against Me. Whoever does not gather with Me scatters.
So I say to you: All kinds of sin and blasphemy (speaking against God) will be forgiven to men. But the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven to men.
Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven them. But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven them, not in this world, and not in the world to come.
Either make the tree good, and its fruit good. Or make the tree corrupt (rotten), and its fruit corrupt (rotten). For the tree is known by its fruit.
O generation of vipers (children of poisonous snakes), how can you speak good things, when you are evil? For out of the abundance (overflow) of the heart the mouth speaks.
A good person brings out good things from the good treasure of the heart. An evil person brings out evil things from the evil treasure.
But I say to you: For every idle (careless) word that men speak, they will give account (answer) for it in the day of judgment.
For by your words you will be justified (shown to be right), and by your words you will be condemned (judged guilty).
Then some of the scribes (teachers of the law) and of the Pharisees answered: Master (Teacher), we want to see a sign from You.
But Jesus answered them: An evil and adulterous (unfaithful to God) generation (people living now) seeks after a sign. But no sign will be given to it, except the sign of the prophet Jonas (Jonah).
For as Jonas (Jonah) was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

The men of Nineveh will rise in judgment with this generation (people living now), and will condemn (judge guilty) it. For they repented (changed their hearts) at the preaching of Jonas (Jonah). And look, One greater than Jonas (Jonah) is here.

The queen of the south will rise up in the judgment with this generation (people living now), and will condemn (judge guilty) it. For she came from the farthest parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. And look, One greater than Solomon is here.
When the unclean spirit has gone out of a man, it walks through dry places, looking for rest, and finds none.
Then the spirit says: I will return to my house that I came out of. When it comes, it finds the house empty, swept, and garnished (decorated).

Then the spirit goes and takes with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself. They enter in and live there. And the last state of that man is worse than the first. That is how it will be for this wicked generation (people living now).
While Jesus was still talking to the people, look, His mother and His brethren (brothers) stood outside, wanting to speak with Him.
Then someone said to Jesus: Look, Your mother and Your brethren (brothers) are standing outside, wanting to speak with You.
But Jesus answered the one who told Him: Who is My mother? And who are My brethren (brothers)?
Jesus stretched out His hand toward His disciples and said: Look at My mother and My brethren (brothers)!
For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, that person is My brother, and sister, and mother.

13.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "Joseph" for "Joses" in 13:55 and dropping "Lord" in 13:51, and it added explanation not in the KJV in 13:26 and 13:52), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his' rendered gender-neutral in v12, v19-23, v57. Parable characters keep their 'his' within each story.

verses.text: The same day Jesus went out of the house, and sat by the sea side.
Great multitudes (large crowds) gathered together to Jesus. So Jesus went into a ship (boat) and sat down. And the whole multitude (crowd) stood on the shore.
Jesus spoke many things to them in parables (stories that teach a lesson). Jesus said: Look, a sower (a man planting seed) went out to sow (plant seed).
As he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side (along the path). The fowls (birds) came and devoured (ate) them up.
Some seeds fell on stony places, where they did not have much earth (soil). Right away they sprang up, because they had no deepness of earth (soil).
When the sun was up, they were scorched (burned). And because they had no root, they withered (dried up) away.
Some seeds fell among thorns. The thorns sprang up and choked them.
But other seeds fell into good ground and brought forth (produced) fruit. Some made a hundredfold (100 times as much), some sixtyfold (60 times), some thirtyfold (30 times).
Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
The disciples came and said to Jesus: Why do You speak to them in parables (stories that teach a lesson)?
Jesus answered them: Because it is given to you to know the mysteries (secrets) of the kingdom of heaven. But to them it is not given.
For whoever has, to them more will be given, and they will have more abundance (more than enough). But whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away from them.
So I speak to them in parables (stories that teach a lesson). Because seeing, they do not see. And hearing, they do not hear, and they do not understand.

In them the prophecy of Esaias (Isaiah) is fulfilled (comes true). It says: By hearing you will hear, and will not understand. And seeing you will see, and will not perceive (understand what you see).

For this people's heart is waxed gross (has become hard and dull). Their ears are dull of hearing. They have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart. Then they might be converted (turn back to God), and I would heal them.
But blessed are your eyes, for they see. And blessed are your ears, for they hear.

For truly I say to you: Many prophets and righteous (right with God) men have desired (wanted) to see the things you see, and have not seen them. They wanted to hear the things you hear, and have not heard them.
So hear the parable (story that teaches a lesson) of the sower (the man planting seed).

When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, then the wicked one (the devil) comes. He catches away what was sown in that person's heart. This is the seed sown by the way side (along the path).
The seed sown into stony places is the person who hears the word, and right away receives it with joy.

Yet that person has no root in themselves, and lasts only for a while. When tribulation (trouble) or persecution (attack for faith) comes because of the word, right away that person is offended (falls away).

The seed sown among the thorns is the person who hears the word. But the care (worry) of this world, and the deceitfulness (lies) of riches, choke the word. And that person becomes unfruitful (has no fruit).

But the seed sown into the good ground is the person who hears the word and understands it. That person bears fruit and brings forth (produces): some a hundredfold (100 times as much), some sixty, some thirty.
Jesus told them another parable (story that teaches a lesson): The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed (planted) good seed in his field.
But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares (weeds) among the wheat, and went his way.
When the blade (plant) had sprung up and brought forth (produced) fruit, then the tares (weeds) appeared also.
So the servants of the householder (owner of the house) came and said to him: Sir, did you not sow (plant) good seed in your field? Where then did the tares (weeds) come from?
He said to them: An enemy has done this. The servants said to him: Do you want us to go and gather them up?
But he said: No. While you gather up the tares (weeds), you might root up the wheat with them.

Let both grow together until the harvest. In the time of harvest I will say to the reapers (workers who cut the grain): Gather together first the tares (weeds), and tie them in bundles to burn them. But gather the wheat into my barn.
Jesus told them another parable (story that teaches a lesson): The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed. A man took it and sowed (planted) it in his field.
It is truly the least (smallest) of all seeds. But when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs (garden plants), and becomes a tree. So the birds of the air come and lodge (rest) in its branches.

Jesus told them another parable (story that teaches a lesson): The kingdom of heaven is like leaven (yeast). A woman took it and hid it in three measures of meal (flour), until all of it was leavened (raised by the yeast).
Jesus spoke all these things to the multitude (crowd) in parables (stories that teach a lesson). Without a parable He did not speak to them.

This happened so that what was spoken by the prophet would be fulfilled (come true). The prophet said: I will open My mouth in parables (stories that teach a lesson). I will tell things that have been kept secret from the foundation (beginning) of the world.
Then Jesus sent the multitude (crowd) away, and went into the house. His disciples came to Jesus and said: Declare (explain) to us the parable (story) of the tares (weeds) of the field.
Jesus answered them: The one who sows (plants) the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world. The good seed are the children of the kingdom. But the tares (weeds) are the children of the wicked one (the devil).
The enemy who sowed (planted) them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the world. And the reapers (workers who cut the grain) are the angels.
So as the tares (weeds) are gathered and burned in the fire, so it will be in the end of this world.
The Son of Man will send out His angels. They will gather out of His kingdom all things that offend (cause sin), and those who do iniquity (sin).
The angels will throw them into a furnace of fire. There will be wailing (loud crying) and gnashing (grinding) of teeth.
Then the righteous (those who are right with God) will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man finds it, he hides it. For joy over it he goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant (a man who buys and sells), looking for goodly (beautiful) pearls.
When he found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was thrown into the sea, and gathered fish of every kind.
When the net was full, they pulled it to shore and sat down. They gathered the good fish into vessels (baskets), but threw the bad away.
That is how it will be at the end of the world. The angels will come out and sever (separate) the wicked from among the just (those who are right with God).
The angels will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be wailing (loud crying) and gnashing (grinding) of teeth.
Jesus said to them: Have you understood all these things? They said to Jesus: Yes, Lord.

Then Jesus said to them: So every scribe (teacher of the law) who is instructed (taught) in the kingdom of heaven is like a man who is a householder (owner of the house). He brings out of his treasure things new and old.
When Jesus had finished these parables (stories that teach a lesson), He left there.

When Jesus came into His own country (hometown), He taught them in their synagogue (meeting house). They were astonished (amazed), and said: Where did this man get this wisdom, and these mighty works?
Is not this the carpenter's son? Is not His mother called Mary? And His brethren (brothers), James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?
And His sisters, are they not all with us? Where then did this man get all these things?

And they were offended in Him (turned away from Him). But Jesus said to them: A prophet is not without honour (respect), except in that prophet's own country (hometown), and in that prophet's own house.
And Jesus did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

14.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "far from land" instead of "in the midst of the sea" in 14:24), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V20 keeps the KJV word 'baskets' and explains it as 'small hand-baskets' (Greek kophinoi), kept distinct from the 'large hampers' (spyrides) of 15:37 and 16:9-10.

verses.text: At that time Herod the tetrarch (ruler over part of a land) heard of the fame (news) of Jesus.
Herod said to his servants: This is John the Baptist. He is risen from the dead. That is why mighty works show themselves in him.
For Herod had taken hold of John, tied him up, and put him in prison. Herod did this for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife.
For John said to Herod: It is not lawful (allowed by the law) for you to have her.
Herod wanted to put John to death, but Herod feared the multitude (crowd), because they counted John as a prophet.
But when Herod's birthday was kept (celebrated), the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod.
So Herod promised with an oath (promise) to give her whatever she would ask.
Her mother had told her ahead of time what to say. So she said: Give me here John Baptist's head in a charger (large platter).
The king was sorry. But for the oath's (promise's) sake, and for the people who sat with him at meat (at the meal), Herod commanded it to be given to her.
Herod sent and beheaded (cut off the head of) John in the prison.
John's head was brought in a charger (large platter), and given to the damsel (girl). And she brought it to her mother.
John's disciples came, took up the body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard of it, He left there by ship (boat) to a desert place, to be alone. When the people heard of it, they followed Jesus on foot out of the cities.
Jesus went out, and saw a great multitude (crowd). Jesus was moved with compassion (deep pity) toward them, and He healed their sick.

When it was evening, His disciples came to Jesus. They said: This is a desert place, and the time is now late. Send the multitude (crowd) away, so they may go into the villages and buy themselves victuals (food).
But Jesus said to them: They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat.
They said to Jesus: We have here only five loaves (of bread), and two fishes.
Jesus said: Bring them here to Me.

Jesus commanded the multitude (crowd) to sit down on the grass. Jesus took the five loaves and the two fishes. Looking up to heaven, He blessed, and broke, and gave the loaves to His disciples. And the disciples gave them to the multitude.
They all ate, and were filled. They took up twelve baskets (small hand-baskets) full of the fragments (pieces) that were left.
Those who had eaten were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
Right away Jesus constrained (made) His disciples get into a ship (boat), and go before Him to the other side, while He sent the multitudes (crowds) away.
When Jesus had sent the multitudes (crowds) away, He went up into a mountain alone to pray. When the evening came, Jesus was there alone.
But the ship (boat) was now in the middle of the sea, tossed with waves. For the wind was contrary (blowing against them).
In the fourth watch of the night (between 3 and 6 in the morning), Jesus went to them, walking on the sea.
When the disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea, they were troubled (afraid). They said: It is a spirit (ghost)! And they cried out for fear.
But right away Jesus spoke to them: Be of good cheer (take heart). It is I. Do not be afraid.
Peter answered Jesus: Lord, if it is You, bid (tell) me to come to You on the water.
Jesus said: Come. When Peter had come down out of the ship (boat), he walked on the water, to go to Jesus.
But when Peter saw the wind boisterous (strong and rough), he was afraid. Beginning to sink, Peter cried out: Lord, save me.
Right away Jesus stretched out His hand, and caught Peter. Jesus said to him: O you of little faith, why did you doubt?
When they had come into the ship (boat), the wind ceased (stopped).
Then those who were in the ship (boat) came and worshipped Jesus. They said: Truly You are the Son of God.
When they had gone over the sea, they came into the land of Gennesaret.
When the men of that place knew it was Jesus, they sent out into all the country around. They brought to Jesus all who were diseased (sick).
They besought (begged) Jesus that they might only touch the hem (edge) of His garment (clothes). And as many as touched were made perfectly whole (completely healed).

15.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. leaving out "or his mother" in 15:6, "draweth nigh unto me with their mouth" in 15:8, and using "Magadan" for "Magdala" in 15:39), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his' rendered gender-neutral in v4-6. V37 keeps the KJV word 'baskets' and explains it as 'large hampers' (Greek spyrides), kept distinct from the 'small hand-baskets' (kophinoi) of 14:20.

verses.text: Then scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees who were from Jerusalem came to Jesus. They said:
Why do Your disciples transgress (break) the tradition (handed-down rules) of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.
But Jesus answered them: Why do you also transgress (break) the commandment of God by your tradition (handed-down rules)?
For God commanded: Honour (respect) your father and mother. And: Whoever curses father or mother, let that person die the death (surely be put to death).
But you say: Whoever says to their father or their mother, It is a gift (given to God), whatever help you might have had from me,
And does not honour (respect) their father or their mother, that person will be free. So you have made the commandment of God of none effect (worthless) by your tradition (handed-down rules).
You hypocrites (pretenders), Esaias (Isaiah) prophesied (spoke God's message) well about you. Isaiah said:
This people draws nigh (comes near) to Me with their mouth, and honours (respects) Me with their lips. But their heart is far from Me.
But in vain (for nothing) they worship Me, teaching for doctrines (teachings) the commandments of men.
Jesus called the multitude (crowd) and said to them: Hear, and understand.
What goes into the mouth does not defile (make unclean) a man. But what comes out of the mouth, this defiles (makes unclean) a man.
Then His disciples came and said to Jesus: Do You know that the Pharisees were offended (upset) after they heard this saying?
But Jesus answered: Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up.
Let them alone. They are blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both will fall into the ditch.
Then Peter answered Jesus: Declare (explain) to us this parable (story that teaches a lesson).
Jesus said: Are you also still without understanding?
Do you not yet understand? Whatever enters in at the mouth goes into the belly (stomach), and is thrown out into the draught (toilet).
But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart. And they defile (make unclean) the man.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries (being unfaithful in marriage), fornications (sexual sins), thefts, false witness (lies about others), blasphemies (speaking against God).
These are the things that defile (make unclean) a man. But to eat with unwashen hands does not defile (make unclean) a man.
Then Jesus went from there, and left for the coasts (land) of Tyre and Sidon.
And look, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts (land). She cried to Jesus: Have mercy on me, O Lord, You Son of David. My daughter is grievously vexed (badly troubled) with a devil (demon).
But Jesus did not answer her a word. His disciples came and besought (begged) Jesus: Send her away, for she cries after us.
But Jesus answered: I am not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
Then she came and worshipped Jesus. She said: Lord, help me.
But Jesus answered: It is not meet (right) to take the children's bread and throw it to dogs.
She said: Truth, Lord. Yet the dogs eat of the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.
Then Jesus answered her: O woman, great is your faith. Let it be done for you just as you want. And her daughter was made whole (healed) from that very hour.
Jesus left there, and came nigh (near) to the sea of Galilee. Jesus went up into a mountain, and sat down there.

Great multitudes (large crowds) came to Jesus. They had with them people who were lame (could not walk well), blind, dumb (could not speak), maimed (missing or crippled body parts), and many others. They laid them down at Jesus' feet, and He healed them.

So the multitude (crowd) wondered (were amazed) when they saw the dumb (those who could not speak) speak, the maimed (crippled) made whole (healed), the lame (those who could not walk well) walk, and the blind see. And they glorified (praised) the God of Israel.

Then Jesus called His disciples to Him and said: I have compassion (deep pity) on the multitude (crowd). They have stayed with Me now three days, and have nothing to eat. I will not send them away fasting (without food), or they may faint (pass out) on the way.
His disciples said to Jesus: Where could we get so much bread in the wilderness (desert), to fill so great a multitude (crowd)?
Jesus said to them: How many loaves (of bread) do you have? They said: Seven, and a few little fishes.
Jesus commanded the multitude (crowd) to sit down on the ground.
Jesus took the seven loaves and the fishes, and gave thanks. He broke them, and gave to His disciples. And the disciples gave to the multitude.
They all ate, and were filled. They took up seven baskets (large hampers) full of the broken meat (leftover food) that was left.
Those who ate were four thousand men, besides women and children.
Jesus sent away the multitude (crowd), and took ship (got into a boat), and came into the coasts (land) of Magdala.

16.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "the Christ" instead of "Jesus the Christ" in 16:20, and it added words not in the KJV in 16:21 such as 'corrupt priests' and 'evil men'), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his' rendered gender-neutral in v24-27. V9-10 keep the KJV word 'baskets' with the small hand-baskets / large hampers distinction of 14:20 and 15:37.

verses.text: The Pharisees with the Sadducees came to Jesus. Tempting (testing) Him, they desired (asked) Him to show them a sign from heaven.
Jesus answered them: When it is evening, you say: It will be fair (good) weather, for the sky is red.

And in the morning you say: It will be foul (stormy) weather today, for the sky is red and lowring (dark and cloudy). O you hypocrites (pretenders), you can discern (read) the face of the sky. But can you not discern (read) the signs of the times?

A wicked and adulterous (unfaithful to God) generation (people living now) seeks after a sign. But no sign will be given to it, except the sign of the prophet Jonas (Jonah). And Jesus left them, and went away.
When His disciples had come to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.
Then Jesus said to them: Take heed (be careful) and beware of the leaven (yeast) of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.
They reasoned (talked it over) among themselves. They said: It is because we have taken no bread.
When Jesus perceived (knew) it, He said to them: O you of little faith, why do you reason (talk it over) among yourselves, because you have brought no bread?
Do you not yet understand? Do you not remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets (small hand-baskets) you took up?
Or the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets (large hampers) you took up?
How is it that you do not understand that I did not speak to you about bread? I told you to beware of the leaven (yeast) of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.
Then they understood. Jesus did not tell them to beware of the leaven (yeast) of bread, but of the doctrine (teaching) of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.
When Jesus came into the coasts (land) of Caesarea Philippi, He asked His disciples: Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?
They said: Some say that You are John the Baptist. Some say Elias (Elijah). And others say Jeremias (Jeremiah), or one of the prophets.
Jesus said to them: But who do you say that I am?
Simon Peter answered: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
Jesus answered him: Blessed are you, Simon Barjona (son of Jonah). For flesh and blood (no human) has not revealed (shown) this to you, but My Father who is in heaven.
And I say also to you: You are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church. And the gates of hell will not prevail (win) against it.
And I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind (forbid) on earth will be bound in heaven. And whatever you loose (allow) on earth will be loosed in heaven.
Then Jesus charged (strongly told) His disciples that they should tell no one that He was Jesus the Christ.

From that time Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem. He must suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes (teachers of the law), and be killed, and be raised again the third day.
Then Peter took Jesus aside, and began to rebuke (scold) Him. Peter said: Be it far from You, Lord. This will not happen to You.
But Jesus turned and said to Peter: Get behind Me, Satan. You are an offence (stumbling block) to Me. For you savour (care about) not the things of God, but the things of men.
Then Jesus said to His disciples: If anyone will come after Me, let them deny themselves (say no to self), and take up their cross, and follow Me.
For whoever will save their life will lose it. And whoever will lose their life for My sake will find it.
For what is a person profited (helped), if they gain the whole world, and lose their own soul? Or what will a person give in exchange for their soul?
For the Son of Man will come in the glory of His Father with His angels. And then He will reward every person according to their works.
Truly I say to you: There are some standing here who will not taste of death (die), until they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.

17.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "your faith is too small" instead of "your unbelief" in 17:20, and "I will put up" instead of "let us make" in 17:4), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: After six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain, apart by themselves.
Jesus was transfigured (changed in appearance) before them. His face shone like the sun, and His raiment (clothes) was white as the light.
And look, Moses and Elias (Elijah) appeared to them, talking with Jesus.
Then Peter answered and said to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You will, let us make here three tabernacles (tents): one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elias (Elijah).

While Peter was still speaking, look, a bright cloud overshadowed (covered) them. And look, a voice came out of the cloud. The voice said: This is My beloved (dearly loved) Son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear Him.
When the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore (very) afraid.
Jesus came and touched them. Jesus said: Arise (get up), and do not be afraid.
When they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no one, except Jesus only.
As they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged (strongly told) them: Tell the vision to no one, until the Son of Man is risen again from the dead.
His disciples asked Jesus: Why then do the scribes (teachers of the law) say that Elias (Elijah) must come first?
Jesus answered them: Elias (Elijah) truly will come first, and restore (make right again) all things.
But I say to you: Elias (Elijah) has come already, and they did not know him. They have done to him whatever they listed (wanted). In the same way the Son of Man will also suffer from them.
Then the disciples understood that Jesus spoke to them about John the Baptist.
When they had come to the multitude (crowd), a man came to Jesus, kneeling down to Him. The man said:
Lord, have mercy on my son. For he is lunatick (has seizures), and sore vexed (suffers badly). Often he falls into the fire, and often into the water.
I brought him to Your disciples, and they could not cure him.
Then Jesus answered: O faithless and perverse (twisted) generation (people living now), how long will I be with you? How long will I suffer (put up with) you? Bring him here to Me.
Jesus rebuked (gave a strong command to) the devil (demon), and it came out of him. And the child was cured from that very hour.
Then the disciples came to Jesus alone, and said: Why could we not cast him out (drive it out)?
