Jesus said to them: Because of your unbelief. For truly I say to you: If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain: Remove (move) from here to yonder (that) place, and it will remove (move). And nothing will be impossible for you.
But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting (going without food).
While they abode (stayed) in Galilee, Jesus said to them: The Son of Man will be betrayed (handed over) into the hands of men.
They will kill Him, and the third day He will be raised again. And the disciples were exceeding (very) sorry.
When they had come to Capernaum, those who received tribute (tax) money came to Peter. They said: Does your Master (Teacher) not pay tribute (tax)?

Peter said: Yes. When Peter came into the house, Jesus prevented (spoke first to) him. Jesus said: What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute (taxes)? From their own children, or from strangers?
Peter said to Jesus: From strangers. Jesus said to him: Then the children are free.

But so that we do not offend (upset) them, go to the sea, and throw in a hook. Take up the fish that comes up first. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a piece of money. Take that, and give it to them for Me and you.

18.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text in places, e.g. leaving out "their trespasses" in 18:35 and "Lord" in 18:26, and it added words in 18:6), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his/himself' rendered gender-neutral in v4, v6.

verses.text: At the same time the disciples came to Jesus. They said: Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
Jesus called a little child to Him, and set the child in the middle of them.
Jesus said: Truly I say to you: Unless you are converted (turned around), and become like little children, you will not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
So whoever humbles themselves like this little child, that person is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever receives one such little child in My name receives Me.

But whoever offends (causes to sin) one of these little ones who believe in Me, it would be better for that person to have a millstone (large heavy stone) hung around their neck, and be drowned in the depth of the sea.
Woe (great trouble) to the world because of offences (things that cause sin)! For offences (things that cause sin) must come. But woe (great trouble) to that man by whom the offence comes!

So if your hand or your foot offends you (causes you to sin), cut them off, and throw them away from you. It is better for you to enter into life halt (crippled) or maimed (missing a body part), than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into everlasting fire.
And if your eye offends you (causes you to sin), pluck it out, and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell fire.
Take heed (be careful) that you do not despise (look down on) one of these little ones. For I say to you: In heaven their angels always behold (see) the face of My Father who is in heaven.
For the Son of Man has come to save what was lost.

What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep, and one of them has gone astray (wandered away), does he not leave the ninety-nine, and go into the mountains, and seek the one that has gone astray (wandered away)?
And if he finds it, truly I say to you: He rejoices more over that sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
In the same way, it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish (be lost).
If your brother trespasses (does wrong) against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother.
But if he will not hear you, then take with you one or two more. So in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established (proven true).

If he neglects (refuses) to hear them, tell it to the church. But if he neglects (refuses) to hear the church, let him be to you as a heathen (person who does not know God) and a publican (tax collector).
Truly I say to you: Whatever you bind (forbid) on earth will be bound in heaven. And whatever you loose (allow) on earth will be loosed in heaven.
Again I say to you: If two of you agree on earth about anything that they ask, it will be done for them by My Father who is in heaven.
For where two or three are gathered together in My name, there I am in the middle of them.
Then Peter came to Jesus and said: Lord, how often will my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Up to seven times?
Jesus said to Peter: I do not say to you, up to seven times. But up to seventy times seven.
So the kingdom of heaven is like a certain king who wanted to take account (settle the money owed) with his servants.
When the king had begun to reckon (count up what was owed), one servant was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents (a huge amount of money).
But the servant did not have enough to pay. So his lord (master) commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
So the servant fell down and worshipped (bowed down to) him. The servant said: Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay you all.
Then the lord (master) of that servant was moved with compassion (deep pity). He loosed (set free) the servant, and forgave him the debt.

But that same servant went out and found one of his fellowservants, who owed him a hundred pence (a small amount of money). He laid hands on him, and took him by the throat. He said: Pay me what you owe.
His fellowservant fell down at his feet, and besought (begged) him: Have patience with me, and I will pay you all.
But he would not. He went and threw him into prison, until he would pay the debt.
When his fellowservants saw what was done, they were very sorry. They came and told their lord (master) all that was done.
Then his lord (master) called him, and said to him: O you wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt, because you desired (begged) me.
Should you not also have had compassion (pity) on your fellowservant, just as I had pity on you?
His lord (master) was wroth (very angry), and delivered (handed) him to the tormentors (jailers who punish), until he would pay all that was due to him.
So My heavenly Father will also do to you, if you do not forgive from your hearts every one his brother their trespasses (wrongs).

19.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "Good Master" in 19:16, "there is none good but one, that is, God" in 19:17, the last clause of 19:9, "from my youth up" in 19:20 and "or wife" in 19:29, and it added words in 19:28), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: When Jesus had finished these sayings, He left Galilee, and came into the coasts (land) of Judaea beyond Jordan.
Great multitudes (large crowds) followed Jesus, and He healed them there.
The Pharisees also came to Jesus, tempting (testing) Him. They said to Him: Is it lawful (allowed by the law) for a man to put away (divorce) his wife for every cause?
Jesus answered them: Have you not read that He who made them at the beginning made them male and female?
And He said: For this cause a man will leave father and mother, and will cleave (hold tight) to his wife. And they twain (two) will be one flesh.
So they are no more twain (two), but one flesh. So what God has joined together, let not man put asunder (pull apart).
They said to Jesus: Why then did Moses command to give a writing of divorcement (written divorce paper), and to put her away (divorce her)?
Jesus said to them: Because of the hardness of your hearts, Moses suffered (allowed) you to put away (divorce) your wives. But from the beginning it was not so.

And I say to you: Whoever puts away (divorces) his wife, except for fornication (sexual sin), and marries another, commits adultery. And whoever marries her who is put away (divorced) commits adultery.
His disciples said to Jesus: If the case of the man is so with his wife, it is not good to marry.
But Jesus said to them: Not all men can receive this saying, except those to whom it is given.

For there are some eunuchs (men who cannot have children) who were born that way from their mother's womb. There are some eunuchs (men who cannot have children) who were made eunuchs (men who cannot have children) by men. And there are eunuchs (men who cannot have children) who have made themselves eunuchs (men who cannot have children) for the kingdom of heaven's sake. Whoever is able to receive it, let them receive it.
Then little children were brought to Jesus, so that He would put His hands on them, and pray. And the disciples rebuked (scolded) the people who brought them.
But Jesus said: Suffer (allow) little children, and forbid them not, to come to Me. For of such is the kingdom of heaven.
Jesus laid His hands on them, and left there.
And look, a man came and said to Jesus: Good Master (Teacher), what good thing will I do, so that I may have eternal life?
Jesus said to him: Why do you call Me good? There is none good but one, that is, God. But if you will enter into life, keep the commandments.

The man said to Jesus: Which ones? Jesus said: You shall do no murder. You shall not commit adultery (be unfaithful in marriage). You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness (lie about others).
Honour (respect) your father and your mother. And, You shall love your neighbour as yourself.
The young man said to Jesus: All these things I have kept from my youth up (since I was young). What do I lack (still need)?
Jesus said to him: If you will be perfect, go and sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. And come and follow Me.
But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful (sad). For he had great possessions (many things he owned).
Then Jesus said to His disciples: Truly I say to you: A rich man will hardly (with great difficulty) enter into the kingdom of heaven.
And again I say to you: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
When His disciples heard it, they were exceedingly (very) amazed. They said: Who then can be saved?
But Jesus beheld (looked at) them, and said to them: With men this is impossible. But with God all things are possible.
Then Peter answered Jesus: Look, we have forsaken (left) all, and followed You. What will we have then?

Jesus said to them: Truly I say to you: In the regeneration (the making of all things new), when the Son of Man sits on the throne of His glory, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

And every one who has forsaken (left) houses, or brethren (brothers), or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for My name's sake, will receive a hundredfold (100 times as much), and will inherit everlasting life.
But many who are first will be last. And the last will be first.

20.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive" in 20:7, "for many be called, but few chosen" in 20:16, and "baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with" in 20:22-23), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'him' rendered gender-neutral in v26-27.

verses.text: For the kingdom of heaven is like a man who is a householder (owner of the house). He went out early in the morning to hire labourers (workers) into his vineyard (grape farm).
He agreed with the labourers (workers) for a penny (a day's pay) a day. Then he sent them into his vineyard (grape farm).
He went out about the third hour (9 in the morning), and saw others standing idle (doing nothing) in the marketplace.
He said to them: You go into the vineyard (grape farm) also, and whatever is right I will give you. And they went their way.
Again he went out about the sixth hour (noon) and the ninth hour (3 in the afternoon), and did the same.
About the eleventh hour (5 in the afternoon) he went out, and found others standing idle (doing nothing). He said to them: Why do you stand here idle (doing nothing) all the day?
They said to him: Because no one has hired us. He said to them: You go into the vineyard (grape farm) also. And whatever is right, that you will receive.
When evening came, the lord (owner) of the vineyard said to his steward (manager): Call the labourers (workers), and give them their hire (pay), beginning from the last to the first.
When those came who were hired about the eleventh hour (5 in the afternoon), every man received a penny (a day's pay).
But when the first came, they supposed (thought) that they would receive more. But every man of them also received a penny (a day's pay).
When they had received it, they murmured (complained) against the goodman (owner) of the house.
They said: These last have wrought (worked) only one hour, and you have made them equal to us. We have borne (carried) the burden and heat of the day.
But he answered one of them: Friend, I do you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a penny (a day's pay)?
Take what is yours, and go your way. I will give to this last man the same as to you.
Is it not lawful (allowed by the law) for me to do what I want with what is mine? Is your eye evil (are you jealous), because I am good?
So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few chosen.
Jesus was going up to Jerusalem. On the way, He took the twelve disciples apart, and said to them:
Look, we go up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be betrayed (handed over) to the chief priests and to the scribes (teachers of the law). They will condemn (judge) Him to death.
They will deliver (hand) Him to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) to mock, and to scourge (whip), and to crucify (nail to a cross) Him. And the third day He will rise again.
Then the mother of Zebedee's children came to Jesus with her sons. She worshipped Jesus, and desired (asked) a certain thing of Him.
Jesus said to her: What do you want? She said to Jesus: Grant (allow) that these my two sons may sit, the one on Your right hand, and the other on the left, in Your kingdom.
But Jesus answered: You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink of the cup that I will drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They said to Jesus: We are able.

Jesus said to them: You will indeed drink of My cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with. But to sit on My right hand, and on My left, is not Mine to give. It will be given to those for whom it is prepared by My Father.
When the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation (anger) against the two brethren (brothers).

But Jesus called them to Him, and said: You know that the princes (rulers) of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) exercise dominion (rule) over them. And those who are great exercise authority over them.
But it will not be so among you. Whoever will be great among you, let that person be your minister (servant).
And whoever will be chief (first) among you, let that person be your servant.
Even as the Son of Man came not to be ministered to (served), but to minister (serve), and to give His life a ransom (the price paid to set people free) for many.
As they left Jericho, a great multitude (large crowd) followed Jesus.
And look, two blind men were sitting by the way side (along the road). When they heard that Jesus passed by, they cried out: Have mercy on us, O Lord, You Son of David.
The multitude (crowd) rebuked (scolded) them, telling them to hold their peace (be quiet). But they cried out even more: Have mercy on us, O Lord, You Son of David.
Jesus stood still, and called them. Jesus said: What do you want Me to do for you?
They said to Jesus: Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
So Jesus had compassion (deep pity) on them, and touched their eyes. Right away their eyes received sight, and they followed Jesus.

21.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "the temple" instead of "the temple of God" in 21:12 and "you are making it" instead of "ye have made it" in 21:13, and it added words in 21:21), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: When they drew nigh (came near) to Jerusalem, and had come to Bethphage, to the mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples.

Jesus said to them: Go into the village over against you (in front of you). Right away you will find an ass (donkey) tied, and a colt (young donkey) with her. Loose (untie) them, and bring them to Me.
If anyone says anything to you, you will say: The Lord has need of them. And right away he will send them.
All this was done so that what was spoken by the prophet would be fulfilled (come true). The prophet said:
Tell the daughter of Sion (Zion): Look, your King comes to you, meek (gentle), and sitting on an ass (donkey), and a colt (young donkey), the foal (baby) of an ass (donkey).
The disciples went, and did as Jesus commanded them.
They brought the ass (donkey) and the colt (young donkey). They put their clothes on them, and they set Jesus on them.
A very great multitude (crowd) spread their garments (clothes) in the way (road). Others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed (spread) them in the way (road).
The multitudes (crowds) that went before, and that followed, cried out: Hosanna (save now) to the Son of David! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna (save now) in the highest!
When Jesus had come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved (stirred up). They said: Who is this?
The multitude (crowd) said: This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee.

Jesus went into the temple of God. Jesus cast out (drove out) all those who sold and bought in the temple. Jesus overthrew (turned over) the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of those who sold doves.
Jesus said to them: It is written: My house will be called the house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves.
The blind and the lame (people who could not walk well) came to Jesus in the temple, and He healed them.

The chief priests and scribes (teachers of the law) saw the wonderful things that Jesus did. They saw the children crying out in the temple: Hosanna (save now) to the Son of David! And they were sore (very) displeased.
They said to Jesus: Do You hear what these say? Jesus said to them: Yes. Have you never read: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings (babies who still nurse) You have perfected praise?
Jesus left them, and went out of the city into Bethany. And He lodged (stayed the night) there.
In the morning, as Jesus returned into the city, He was hungry.

Jesus saw a fig tree by the way (road). He came to it, and found nothing on it, but leaves only. Jesus said to it: Let no fruit grow on you from now on for ever. And presently (right away) the fig tree withered (dried up) away.
When the disciples saw it, they marvelled (were amazed). They said: How soon the fig tree has withered (dried up) away!

Jesus answered them: Truly I say to you: If you have faith, and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree. But also if you say to this mountain, Be removed, and be thrown into the sea, it will be done.
And all things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.

When Jesus had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to Him as He was teaching. They said: By what authority do You do these things? And who gave You this authority?
Jesus answered them: I also will ask you one thing. If you tell Me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.

The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven, or from men? They reasoned (talked it over) with themselves. They said: If we say, From heaven, He will say to us: Why then did you not believe him?
But if we say, From men, we fear the people. For all hold John as a prophet.
They answered Jesus: We cannot tell. And Jesus said to them: Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
But what do you think? A certain man had two sons. He came to the first, and said: Son, go work today in my vineyard (grape farm).
The son answered: I will not. But afterward he repented (changed his mind), and went.
The man came to the second son, and said the same. And he answered: I go, sir. But he did not go.

Which of the twain (two) did the will of his father? They said to Jesus: The first. Jesus said to them: Truly I say to you: The publicans (tax collectors) and the harlots (prostitutes) go into the kingdom of God before you.

For John came to you in the way of righteousness (being right with God), and you did not believe him. But the publicans (tax collectors) and the harlots (prostitutes) believed him. And you, when you had seen it, did not repent (change your hearts) afterward, so that you might believe him.

Hear another parable (story that teaches a lesson): There was a certain householder (owner of the house) who planted a vineyard (grape farm). He hedged (fenced) it around, and dug a winepress (place to crush grapes) in it, and built a tower. He let it out (rented it) to husbandmen (farmers), and went into a far country.
When the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen (farmers), so they might receive the fruits of it.
The husbandmen (farmers) took his servants. They beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
Again, he sent other servants, more than the first. And they did the same to them.
But last of all he sent his son to them. He said: They will reverence (respect) my son.
But when the husbandmen (farmers) saw the son, they said among themselves: This is the heir (the one who will own it all). Come, let us kill him, and let us seize (take) his inheritance.
They caught him, and threw him out of the vineyard (grape farm), and slew (killed) him.
So when the lord (owner) of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those husbandmen (farmers)?
They said to Jesus: He will miserably destroy those wicked men. He will let out (rent) his vineyard to other husbandmen (farmers), who will render (give) him the fruits in their seasons.

Jesus said to them: Did you never read in the scriptures: The stone which the builders rejected, the same has become the head of the corner (the most important stone). This is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous (wonderful) in our eyes?
So I say to you: The kingdom of God will be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth (producing) its fruits.
Whoever falls on this stone will be broken. But on whomever it falls, it will grind them to powder.
When the chief priests and Pharisees had heard His parables (stories that teach a lesson), they perceived (understood) that He spoke about them.
But when they sought (tried) to lay hands on Jesus, they feared the multitude (crowd), because the people took Jesus for a prophet.

22.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "angels" instead of "angels of God" in 22:30, "under your feet" instead of "thy footstool" in 22:44, and dropping "take him away" in 22:13), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Jesus answered and spoke to them again by parables (stories that teach a lesson). Jesus said:
The kingdom of heaven is like a certain king who made a marriage (wedding feast) for his son.
He sent out his servants to call those who were bidden (invited) to the wedding. But they would not come.

Again, he sent out other servants. He said: Tell those who are bidden (invited): Look, I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and my fatlings (fattened animals) are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the marriage (wedding feast).
But they made light of it (did not care), and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise (business).
The remnant (the rest) took his servants, and entreated them spitefully (treated them cruelly), and slew (killed) them.
But when the king heard of it, he was wroth (very angry). He sent out his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.
Then the king said to his servants: The wedding is ready, but those who were bidden (invited) were not worthy.
So go into the highways (main roads). And as many as you find, bid (invite) them to the marriage (wedding feast).
So those servants went out into the highways (main roads), and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good. And the wedding was furnished (filled) with guests.
When the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who did not have on a wedding garment (wedding clothes).
The king said to him: Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment (wedding clothes)? And the man was speechless.
Then the king said to the servants: Bind (tie) him hand and foot, and take him away, and throw him into outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing (grinding) of teeth.
For many are called, but few are chosen.
Then the Pharisees went and took counsel (made plans) how they might entangle (trap) Jesus in His talk.

They sent out their disciples to Jesus with the Herodians (followers of King Herod). They said: Master (Teacher), we know that You are true, and teach the way of God in truth. You do not care about anyone's opinion, for You regard not the person of men (do not favor anyone).
So tell us, what do You think? Is it lawful (allowed by the law) to give tribute (tax) to Caesar, or not?
But Jesus perceived (knew) their wickedness. Jesus said: Why do you tempt (test) Me, you hypocrites (pretenders)?
Show Me the tribute (tax) money. And they brought to Jesus a penny (a coin worth a day's pay).
Jesus said to them: Whose is this image (picture) and superscription (writing)?
They said to Jesus: Caesar's. Then Jesus said to them: So render (give) to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.
When they had heard these words, they marvelled (were amazed). They left Jesus, and went their way.
The same day the Sadducees came to Jesus. They say that there is no resurrection (rising from the dead). They asked Him:
Master (Teacher), Moses said: If a man dies, having no children, his brother will marry his wife, and raise up seed (children) for his brother.
Now there were with us seven brethren (brothers). The first, when he had married a wife, deceased (died). He had no issue (children), so he left his wife to his brother.
The same happened to the second also, and the third, up to the seventh.
And last of all the woman died also.
So in the resurrection (rising from the dead), whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.
Jesus answered them: You do err (are wrong), not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.
For in the resurrection (rising from the dead) they do not marry, nor are given in marriage. But they are like the angels of God in heaven.
But about the resurrection (rising) of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God? God said:
I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
When the multitude (crowd) heard this, they were astonished (amazed) at His doctrine (teaching).
But when the Pharisees had heard that Jesus had put the Sadducees to silence (made them quiet), they gathered together.
Then one of them, who was a lawyer (expert in God's law), asked Jesus a question, tempting (testing) Him. He said:
Master (Teacher), which is the great commandment in the law?
Jesus said to him: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind.
This is the first and great commandment.
And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbour as yourself.
On these two commandments hang (depend) all the law and the prophets.
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them:
What do you think of Christ? Whose son is He? They said to Jesus: The son of David.
Jesus said to them: How then does David in spirit (moved by the Spirit) call Him Lord? David said:
The LORD said to my Lord: Sit on My right hand, until I make Your enemies Your footstool (a place to rest Your feet).
If David then calls Him Lord, how is He his son?
No one was able to answer Jesus a word. And from that day on, no one durst (dared) ask Him any more questions.

23.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "even Christ" in 23:8 and "grievous to be borne" in 23:4, and it added words in 23:35 and 23:37 such as 'bronze altar' and 'in love'), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/himself' rendered gender-neutral in v12, v15-18.

verses.text: Then Jesus spoke to the multitude (crowd), and to His disciples.
Jesus said: The scribes (teachers of the law) and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat (teach Moses' law).
So whatever they bid (tell) you to observe (keep), that observe and do. But do not do what they do. For they say, and do not do.
For they bind (tie up) heavy burdens (loads) that are grievous (hard) to be borne (carried), and lay them on men's shoulders. But they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.

But they do all their works to be seen by men. They make broad (wide) their phylacteries (little boxes holding Bible verses, worn on the body), and enlarge the borders (fringes) of their garments (clothes).
They love the uppermost rooms (best places) at feasts, and the chief (best) seats in the synagogues (meeting houses).
And they love greetings in the markets, and to be called by men: Rabbi, Rabbi (Teacher, Teacher).
But do not be called Rabbi (Teacher). For one is your Master (Teacher), even Christ. And all of you are brethren (brothers).
And call no man your father on the earth. For one is your Father, who is in heaven.
Do not be called masters (teachers). For one is your Master (Teacher), even Christ.
But whoever is greatest among you will be your servant.
Whoever exalts (lifts up) themselves will be abased (brought low). And whoever humbles themselves will be exalted (lifted up).

But woe (great trouble) to you, scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, hypocrites (pretenders)! For you shut up the kingdom of heaven against men. You do not go in yourselves, and you do not let those who are entering go in.

Woe (great trouble) to you, scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, hypocrites (pretenders)! For you devour (eat up) widows' houses, and for a pretence (to look good) make long prayers. So you will receive the greater damnation (punishment).

Woe (great trouble) to you, scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, hypocrites (pretenders)! For you go around sea and land to make one proselyte (convert). When that person is made, you make them twofold (two times) more the child of hell than yourselves.
Woe (great trouble) to you, you blind guides! You say: Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing. But whoever swears by the gold of the temple, that person is a debtor (bound by the promise)!
You fools and blind! For which is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifies (makes holy) the gold?
And you say: Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing. But whoever swears by the gift that is on it, that person is guilty (bound by the promise).
You fools and blind! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies (makes holy) the gift?
So whoever swears by the altar, swears by it, and by all things on it.
And whoever swears by the temple, swears by it, and by Him who dwells (lives) in it.
And whoever swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God, and by Him who sits on it.

Woe (great trouble) to you, scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, hypocrites (pretenders)! For you pay tithe (a tenth part) of mint and anise and cummin (small garden herbs). But you have left undone the weightier (more important) matters of the law: judgment (fairness), mercy, and faith. These you ought to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
You blind guides, who strain at (strain out) a gnat (tiny bug), and swallow a camel!

Woe (great trouble) to you, scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, hypocrites (pretenders)! For you make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter (plate). But inside they are full of extortion (stealing by force) and excess (no self-control).
You blind Pharisee, first clean what is inside the cup and platter (plate), so that the outside of them may be clean also.

Woe (great trouble) to you, scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, hypocrites (pretenders)! For you are like whited sepulchres (tombs painted white). They indeed look beautiful on the outside, but inside they are full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.
In the same way, you also look righteous (right with God) to men on the outside. But inside you are full of hypocrisy (pretending) and iniquity (sin).

Woe (great trouble) to you, scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, hypocrites (pretenders)! Because you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish (decorate) the sepulchres (tombs) of the righteous.
And you say: If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers (sharers) with them in the blood of the prophets.
So you are witnesses against yourselves, that you are the children of those who killed the prophets.
Fill up then the measure (the full amount) of your fathers.
You serpents (snakes), you generation of vipers (children of poisonous snakes), how can you escape the damnation (punishment) of hell?

So look, I send to you prophets, and wise men, and scribes (teachers of the law). Some of them you will kill and crucify (nail to a cross). And some of them you will scourge (whip) in your synagogues (meeting houses), and persecute (attack) them from city to city.
So upon you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom you slew (killed) between the temple and the altar.
Truly I say to you: All these things will come upon this generation (people living now).

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets, and stone those who are sent to you! How often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!
Look, your house is left to you desolate (empty and ruined).
For I say to you: You will not see Me from now on, until you say: Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.

26.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "blood of the agreement" instead of "blood of the new testament" in 26:28, and leaving out "and the scribes" in 26:3 and "yet found they none" in 26:60), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: When Jesus had finished all these sayings, He said to His disciples:
You know that after two days is the feast of the passover (feast of freedom from Egypt). And the Son of Man is betrayed (handed over) to be crucified (nailed to a cross).
Then the chief priests, and the scribes (teachers of the law), and the elders of the people assembled together at the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
They consulted (made plans) so they might take Jesus by subtilty (trickery), and kill Him.
But they said: Not on the feast day, or there may be an uproar (riot) among the people.
Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper (a man with a skin disease),
A woman came to Jesus with an alabaster box (a stone jar) of very precious ointment (perfumed oil). She poured it on His head, as He sat at meat (at the meal).
But when His disciples saw it, they had indignation (were angry). They said: Why this waste?
For this ointment (perfumed oil) might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.
When Jesus understood it, He said to them: Why do you trouble the woman? For she has wrought (done) a good work for Me.
For you have the poor always with you. But you do not have Me always.
For in pouring this ointment (perfumed oil) on My body, she did it for My burial.
Truly I say to you: Wherever this gospel (good news) is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told, for a memorial (a way to remember) of her.
Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests.
Judas said to them: What will you give me, if I deliver (hand) Him to you? And they covenanted (agreed) with him for thirty pieces of silver.
From that time Judas sought (looked for) an opportunity to betray (hand over) Jesus.

On the first day of the feast of unleavened bread (bread made without yeast), the disciples came to Jesus. They said to Him: Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the passover (feast of freedom from Egypt)?

Jesus said: Go into the city to a certain man, and say to him: The Master (Teacher) says: My time is at hand (near). I will keep the passover (feast of freedom from Egypt) at your house with My disciples.
The disciples did as Jesus had appointed (told) them. And they made ready the passover (feast of freedom from Egypt).
When the evening had come, Jesus sat down with the twelve.
As they were eating, Jesus said: Truly I say to you: One of you will betray (hand over) Me.
They were exceeding (very) sorrowful (sad). Every one of them began to say to Jesus: Lord, is it I?
Jesus answered: The one who dips his hand with Me in the dish, the same will betray (hand over) Me.
The Son of Man goes as it is written about Him. But woe (great trouble) to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed (handed over)! It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.
Then Judas, who betrayed (handed over) Him, answered: Master (Teacher), is it I? Jesus said to him: You have said it.
As they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and broke it. He gave it to the disciples, and said: Take, eat. This is My body.
Jesus took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them. Jesus said: Drink all of it.
For this is My blood of the new testament (new agreement), which is shed for many for the remission (forgiveness) of sins.
But I say to you: I will not drink from now on of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in My Father's kingdom.
When they had sung a hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them: All of you will be offended (fall away) because of Me this night. For it is written: I will smite (strike) the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.
But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.
Peter answered Jesus: Though all men will be offended (fall away) because of You, yet I will never be offended (fall away).
Jesus said to Peter: Truly I say to you: This night, before the cock (rooster) crows, you will deny (say you do not know) Me thrice (three times).
Peter said to Jesus: Even if I must die with You, I will not deny (say I do not know) You. And all the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to the disciples: Sit here, while I go and pray yonder (over there).
Jesus took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee. He began to be sorrowful (sad) and very heavy (troubled).
Then Jesus said to them: My soul is exceeding (very) sorrowful (sad), even to death. Tarry (stay) here, and watch with Me.
Jesus went a little farther, and fell on His face, and prayed: O My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Nevertheless (but) not as I will, but as You will.
Jesus came to the disciples, and found them asleep. Jesus said to Peter: What, could you not watch with Me one hour?
Watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh (body) is weak.
Jesus went away again the second time, and prayed: O My Father, if this cup may not pass away from Me unless I drink it, Your will be done.
Jesus came and found them asleep again, for their eyes were heavy.
Jesus left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words.
Then Jesus came to His disciples, and said to them: Sleep on now, and take your rest. Look, the hour is at hand (near), and the Son of Man is betrayed (handed over) into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us be going. Look, he is at hand (near) who betrays (hands over) Me.
While Jesus was still speaking, lo (look), Judas, one of the twelve, came. With him was a great multitude (crowd) with swords and staves (clubs), from the chief priests and elders of the people.
Now the one who betrayed (handed over) Jesus gave them a sign. He said: Whoever I kiss, that is He. Hold Him fast (tight).
Right away Judas came to Jesus, and said: Hail (greetings), Master (Teacher). And Judas kissed Him.
Jesus said to him: Friend, why have you come? Then they came, and laid hands on Jesus, and took Him.
And look, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword. He struck a servant of the high priest, and smote off (cut off) his ear.
Then Jesus said to him: Put your sword back into its place. For all who take the sword will perish (die) with the sword.
Do you think that I cannot now pray to My Father, and He will presently (right away) give Me more than twelve legions (armies) of angels?
But how then would the scriptures be fulfilled (come true), that it must happen this way?

In that same hour Jesus said to the multitudes (crowds): Have you come out as against a thief, with swords and staves (clubs) to take Me? I sat daily with you teaching in the temple, and you did not lay hold on Me.
But all this was done so that the scriptures of the prophets would be fulfilled (come true). Then all the disciples forsook (left) Jesus, and fled (ran away).
Those who had laid hold on Jesus led Him away to Caiaphas the high priest. There the scribes (teachers of the law) and the elders were assembled (gathered).
But Peter followed Jesus afar off (from a distance) to the high priest's palace. He went in, and sat with the servants, to see the end.
Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council (Jewish court) sought (looked for) false witness (lies) against Jesus, to put Him to death.
But they found none. Yes, though many false witnesses (liars) came, still they found none. At the last two false witnesses (liars) came.
They said: This fellow said: I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.
The high priest arose (stood up), and said to Jesus: Do You answer nothing? What is it that these witness against You?
But Jesus held His peace (stayed quiet). The high priest answered Him: I adjure (command) You by the living God: Tell us whether You are the Christ, the Son of God.
Jesus said to him: You have said it. Nevertheless (but) I say to you: Hereafter (from now on) you will see the Son of Man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

Then the high priest rent (tore) his clothes. He said: He has spoken blasphemy (speaking against God). What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you have heard His blasphemy (speaking against God).
What do you think? They answered: He is guilty of death (deserves to die).
Then they spit in His face, and buffeted (punched) Him. Others smote (struck) Him with the palms of their hands.
They said: Prophesy (tell us by God's power) to us, You Christ: Who is the one who smote (struck) You?
Now Peter sat without (outside) in the palace. A damsel (servant girl) came to him and said: You also were with Jesus of Galilee.
But Peter denied it before them all. He said: I do not know what you are saying.
When Peter had gone out into the porch, another maid (servant girl) saw him. She said to those who were there: This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth.
Again Peter denied it with an oath (promise to God): I do not know the man.
After a while those who stood by came to Peter. They said: Surely you also are one of them. For your speech bewrays you (gives you away).
Then Peter began to curse and to swear (make oaths). He said: I do not know the man. And right away the cock (rooster) crew (crowed).
Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said to him: Before the cock (rooster) crows, you will deny (say you do not know) Me thrice (three times). And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
Jesus went out, and left the temple. His disciples came to Jesus to show Him the buildings of the temple.
Jesus said to them: Do you not see all these things? Truly I say to you: Not one stone will be left here on another, that will not be thrown down.
As Jesus sat on the mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. They said: Tell us, when will these things be? And what will be the sign of Your coming, and of the end of the world?
Jesus answered them: Take heed (be careful) that no one deceives (fools) you.
For many will come in My name, saying, I am Christ. And they will deceive (fool) many.
You will hear of wars and rumours (reports) of wars. See that you are not troubled. For all these things must come to pass (happen), but the end is not yet.

For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be famines (times of no food), and pestilences (deadly sicknesses), and earthquakes, in divers (many different) places.
All these are the beginning of sorrows (great pains).
Then they will deliver you up (hand you over) to be afflicted (made to suffer), and will kill you. And you will be hated by all nations for My name's sake.
Then many will be offended (fall away), and will betray (hand over) one another, and will hate one another.
And many false prophets will rise, and will deceive (fool) many.
Because iniquity (sin) will abound (grow everywhere), the love of many will wax cold (grow cold).
But whoever endures (keeps on faithful) to the end, that person will be saved.
And this gospel (good news) of the kingdom will be preached in all the world for a witness to all nations. And then the end will come.
So when you see the abomination of desolation (the hateful thing that brings ruin), spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (whoever reads, let them understand),
Then let those who are in Judaea flee (run away) into the mountains.
Let whoever is on the housetop not come down to take anything out of their house.
And let whoever is in the field not return back to take their clothes.
Woe (great trouble) to those who are with child (pregnant), and to those who give suck (nurse babies) in those days!
But pray that your flight (escape) is not in the winter, or on the sabbath day (day of rest).
For then there will be great tribulation (trouble), such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever will be.
Unless those days were shortened, no flesh (person) would be saved. But for the elect's (chosen people's) sake those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you, Lo (look), here is Christ, or there, do not believe it.
For false Christs and false prophets will arise. They will show great signs and wonders. So that, if it were possible, they would deceive (fool) the very elect (chosen people).
Look, I have told you before.
So if they say to you, Look, He is in the desert, do not go out. Look, He is in the secret chambers (hidden rooms), do not believe it.
For as the lightning comes out of the east, and shines even to the west, so also will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For wherever the carcase (dead body) is, there the eagles will be gathered together.

Right away after the tribulation (trouble) of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give her light. The stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven. And then all the tribes of the earth will mourn (be very sad). And they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
He will send His angels with a great sound of a trumpet. And they will gather together His elect (chosen people) from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
Now learn a parable (story that teaches a lesson) of the fig tree. When its branch is still tender (soft), and puts out leaves, you know that summer is nigh (near).
So likewise you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.
Truly I say to you: This generation will not pass, until all these things are fulfilled (come true).
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will not pass away.
But of that day and hour no one knows, no, not the angels of heaven, but My Father only.
But as the days of Noe (Noah) were, so also will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For as in the days that were before the flood, they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe (Noah) entered into the ark (big boat).
They did not know until the flood came, and took them all away. So also will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Then two will be in the field. The one will be taken, and the other left.
Two women will be grinding at the mill (grain grinder). The one will be taken, and the other left.
So watch. For you do not know what hour your Lord comes.

But know this: If the goodman (owner) of the house had known in what watch (time of night) the thief would come, he would have watched. He would not have suffered (allowed) his house to be broken into.
So you also be ready. For in an hour when you think not, the Son of Man comes.
Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord (master) has made ruler over his household, to give them meat (food) in due season (at the right time)?
Blessed is that servant, whom his lord (master) will find so doing when he comes.
Truly I say to you: He will make him ruler over all his goods.
But if that evil servant says in his heart, My lord (master) delays his coming,
And begins to smite (hit) his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken,
The lord (master) of that servant will come in a day when he does not look for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of.
He will cut him asunder (cut him in pieces), and appoint (give) him his portion (place) with the hypocrites (pretenders). There will be weeping and gnashing (grinding) of teeth.

verses.text: Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins (young women not yet married). They took their lamps, and went out to meet the bridegroom (the man getting married).
Five of them were wise, and five were foolish.
Those who were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them.
But the wise took oil in their vessels (jars) with their lamps.
While the bridegroom tarried (was slow to come), they all slumbered (got sleepy) and slept.
At midnight there was a cry made: Look, the bridegroom comes. Go out to meet him.
Then all those virgins (young women) arose (got up), and trimmed (got ready) their lamps.
The foolish said to the wise: Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are gone out.
But the wise answered: Not so. Otherwise there will not be enough for us and you. But go instead to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.
While they went to buy, the bridegroom came. Those who were ready went in with him to the marriage (wedding feast). And the door was shut.
Afterward the other virgins (young women) came also. They said: Lord, Lord, open to us.
But he answered: Truly I say to you: I do not know you.
So watch. For you know neither the day nor the hour when the Son of Man comes.
For the kingdom of heaven is like a man traveling into a far country. He called his own servants, and delivered (gave) his goods to them.
To one he gave five talents (huge amounts of money), to another two, and to another one. He gave to every man according to his several (own) ability. And right away he took his journey.
Then he who had received the five talents (huge amounts of money) went and traded with them, and made another five talents (huge amounts of money).
In the same way, he who had received two also gained another two.
But he who had received one went and dug in the earth, and hid his lord's (master's) money.
After a long time the lord (master) of those servants came, and reckoned (settled the money) with them.

So he who had received five talents (huge amounts of money) came and brought another five talents (huge amounts of money). He said: Lord (Master), you delivered (gave) to me five talents (huge amounts of money). Look, I have gained five talents (huge amounts of money) more besides them.
His lord (master) said to him: Well done, you good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things. I will make you ruler over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord (master).

He also who had received two talents (huge amounts of money) came and said: Lord (Master), you delivered (gave) to me two talents (huge amounts of money). Look, I have gained two other talents (huge amounts of money) besides them.
His lord (master) said to him: Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things. I will make you ruler over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord (master).

Then he who had received the one talent (a huge amount of money) came and said: Lord (Master), I knew you, that you are a hard man. You reap (harvest) where you have not sown (planted), and gather where you have not strawed (scattered seed).
I was afraid, and went and hid your talent (a huge amount of money) in the earth. Lo (look), there you have what is yours.
His lord (master) answered him: You wicked and slothful (lazy) servant. You knew that I reap (harvest) where I did not sow (plant), and gather where I have not strawed (scattered seed).
So you ought to have put my money with the exchangers (bankers). Then at my coming I would have received my own with usury (interest).
So take the talent (a huge amount of money) from him, and give it to him who has ten talents (huge amounts of money).
For to every one who has, more will be given, and they will have abundance (more than enough). But from the one who does not have, even what they have will be taken away.
Throw the unprofitable (useless) servant into outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing (grinding) of teeth.
When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the holy angels with Him, then He will sit on the throne of His glory.
Before Him will be gathered all nations. He will separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats.
He will set the sheep on His right hand, but the goats on the left.
Then the King will say to those on His right hand: Come, you blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation (beginning) of the world.
For I was hungry, and you gave Me meat (food). I was thirsty, and you gave Me drink. I was a stranger, and you took Me in.
I was naked, and you clothed Me. I was sick, and you visited Me. I was in prison, and you came to Me.
Then the righteous (those who are right with God) will answer Him: Lord, when did we see You hungry, and fed You? Or thirsty, and gave You drink?
When did we see You a stranger, and took You in? Or naked, and clothed You?
Or when did we see You sick, or in prison, and came to You?
The King will answer them: Truly I say to you: Inasmuch as (since) you have done it to one of the least of these My brethren (brothers), you have done it to Me.
Then He will also say to those on the left hand: Depart from Me, you cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry, and you gave Me no meat (food). I was thirsty, and you gave Me no drink.
I was a stranger, and you did not take Me in. I was naked, and you did not clothe Me. I was sick, and in prison, and you did not visit Me.
Then they will also answer Him: Lord, when did we see You hungry, or athirst (thirsty), or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to (serve) You?
Then He will answer them: Truly I say to you: Inasmuch as (since) you did not do it to one of the least of these, you did not do it to Me.
And these will go away into everlasting punishment. But the righteous (those who are right with God) will go into life eternal.

verses.text: When the morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel (made plans) against Jesus to put Him to death.
When they had bound (tied up) Jesus, they led Him away, and delivered (handed) Him to Pontius Pilate the governor.

Then Judas, who had betrayed (handed over) Jesus, saw that Jesus was condemned (judged guilty). Judas repented himself (was sorry), and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.
Judas said: I have sinned, because I have betrayed (handed over) the innocent blood. They said: What is that to us? See to that yourself.
Judas threw down the pieces of silver in the temple, and left. He went and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver pieces, and said: It is not lawful (allowed by the law) to put them into the treasury (temple money box), because it is the price of blood.
They took counsel (made plans), and with the silver they bought the potter's field, to bury strangers in.
So that field was called The field of blood, to this day.

Then what was spoken by Jeremy (Jeremiah) the prophet was fulfilled (came true). He said: And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of Him that was valued, whom the children of Israel valued.
And they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord appointed (told) me.
Jesus stood before the governor. The governor asked Him: Are You the King of the Jews? Jesus said to him: You say it.
When Jesus was accused by the chief priests and elders, He answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to Jesus: Do You not hear how many things they witness against You?
But Jesus answered him not even one word. So the governor marvelled (was amazed) greatly.
Now at that feast the governor was wont (used) to release to the people one prisoner, whoever they wanted.
They had then a notable (well-known) prisoner, called Barabbas.
So when they were gathered together, Pilate said to them: Who do you want me to release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?
For Pilate knew that because of envy (jealousy) they had delivered (handed) Jesus over.

When Pilate was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent a message to him. She said: Have nothing to do with that just (good and innocent) man. For I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of Him.
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude (crowd) to ask for Barabbas, and to destroy Jesus.
The governor answered them: Which of the twain (two) do you want me to release to you? They said: Barabbas.
Pilate said to them: What will I do then with Jesus who is called Christ? They all said to him: Let Him be crucified (nailed to a cross).
The governor said: Why, what evil has He done? But they cried out even more: Let Him be crucified (nailed to a cross).

When Pilate saw that he could prevail (win) nothing, but that a tumult (riot) was starting instead, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude (crowd). Pilate said: I am innocent of the blood of this just (good and innocent) person. See to it yourselves.
Then all the people answered: His blood be on us, and on our children.
Then Pilate released Barabbas to them. When he had scourged (whipped) Jesus, he delivered (handed) Him to be crucified (nailed to a cross).
Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall (the governor's hall). They gathered to Him the whole band (group) of soldiers.
They stripped Him, and put a scarlet (bright red) robe on Him.

When they had platted (woven) a crown of thorns, they put it on His head, and a reed (stick) in His right hand. They bowed the knee before Him, and mocked Him. They said: Hail (greetings), King of the Jews!
They spit on Him, and took the reed (stick), and smote (struck) Him on the head.
After they had mocked Him, they took the robe off Him, and put His own raiment (clothes) on Him. And they led Him away to crucify (nail to a cross) Him.
As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, named Simon. They compelled (forced) him to bear (carry) His cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull.
They gave Jesus vinegar to drink, mingled (mixed) with gall (bitter liquid). When He had tasted it, He would not drink.

They crucified (nailed to a cross) Him, and parted (divided) His garments (clothes), casting lots (a game of chance to decide). This was so that what was spoken by the prophet would be fulfilled (come true): They parted (divided) My garments (clothes) among them, and for My vesture (robe) they cast lots.
Sitting down, they watched Him there.
They set up over His head His accusation (the charge against Him) written: THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
Then two thieves were crucified (nailed to crosses) with Him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.
Those who passed by reviled (insulted) Him, wagging (shaking) their heads.
They said: You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days, save Yourself. If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross.
In the same way the chief priests also mocked Him, with the scribes (teachers of the law) and elders. They said:
He saved others. Himself He cannot save. If He is the King of Israel, let Him now come down from the cross, and we will believe Him.
He trusted in God. Let God deliver (rescue) Him now, if God will have Him. For He said: I am the Son of God.
The thieves also, who were crucified (nailed to crosses) with Him, cast the same in His teeth (insulted Him the same way).
Now from the sixth hour (noon) there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour (3 in the afternoon).
About the ninth hour (3 in the afternoon) Jesus cried with a loud voice: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? That is to say: My God, My God, why have You forsaken (left) Me?
Some of those who stood there, when they heard that, said: This man calls for Elias (Elijah).
Right away one of them ran, and took a spunge (sponge), and filled it with vinegar. He put it on a reed (stick), and gave Him to drink.
The rest said: Let it be. Let us see whether Elias (Elijah) will come to save Him.
Jesus, when He had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost (gave up His spirit).
And look, the veil (curtain) of the temple was rent (torn) in twain (two) from the top to the bottom. The earth did quake (shake), and the rocks rent (split).
The graves were opened. And many bodies of the saints (holy people) who slept (had died) arose.
They came out of the graves after His resurrection (rising from the dead), and went into the holy city, and appeared to many.

Now when the centurion (army officer over 100 soldiers), and those who were with him watching Jesus, saw the earthquake and the things that were done, they feared greatly. They said: Truly this was the Son of God.
Many women were there beholding (watching) afar off (from a distance). They had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to (serving) Him.
Among them was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee's children.
When the evening came, a rich man of Arimathaea came, named Joseph. He himself was also Jesus' disciple.
Joseph went to Pilate, and begged for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered (given to him).
When Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
He laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn (cut) out in the rock. He rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre (tomb), and left.
Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting over against (across from) the sepulchre (tomb).
The next day, which followed the day of the preparation (the day before the sabbath), the chief priests and Pharisees came together to Pilate.
They said: Sir, we remember that that deceiver (liar) said, while He was still alive: After three days I will rise again.

So command that the sepulchre (tomb) be made sure (safe) until the third day. Otherwise His disciples may come by night, and steal Him away, and say to the people: He is risen from the dead. Then the last error (lie) will be worse than the first.
Pilate said to them: You have a watch (guard of soldiers). Go your way. Make it as sure (safe) as you can.
So they went, and made the sepulchre (tomb) sure (safe), sealing the stone, and setting a watch (guard of soldiers).
In the end of the sabbath (day of rest), as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the sepulchre (tomb).
And look, there was a great earthquake. For the angel of the Lord descended (came down) from heaven. The angel came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat on it.
His countenance (face) was like lightning, and his raiment (clothes) was white as snow.
For fear of him the keepers (guards) did shake, and became as dead men.
The angel answered the women: Do not fear. For I know that you seek (are looking for) Jesus, who was crucified (nailed to a cross).
He is not here. For He is risen, as He said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
Go quickly, and tell His disciples that He is risen from the dead. And look, He goes before you into Galilee. There you will see Him. Lo (look), I have told you.
They left the sepulchre (tomb) quickly with fear and great joy. And they ran to bring His disciples word.
As they went to tell His disciples, look, Jesus met them. Jesus said: All hail (greetings). They came and held Him by the feet, and worshipped Him.
Then Jesus said to them: Do not be afraid. Go tell My brethren (brothers) to go into Galilee, and there they will see Me.
While the women were going, look, some of the watch (guard of soldiers) came into the city. They showed the chief priests all the things that were done.
When the chief priests were assembled (gathered) with the elders, and had taken counsel (made plans), they gave large money to the soldiers.
